identity.name: Panthère de Cartier

case.bezel: polished bezel integrated into the quilted-link bracelet

identity.one_liner: An integrated quilted-link bracelet watch that defined 1980s Cartier, revived in 2017 after roughly two decades out of the catalog.

narrative.story: Cartier launched the Panthère de Cartier in 1983, building the case and its flat quilted-link bracelet as one integrated piece rather than a case with a separate strap — a design decision shared with the sports-watch wave that followed the Royal Oak and Nautilus, though styled toward Cartier's own jewelry-house identity rather than a tool-watch one. Cartier discontinued the line for roughly two decades before reviving it in 2017, reintroducing the same integrated-bracelet silhouette to a generation that had mostly known Cartier through the Tank and Santos.
narrative.collector_notes: Vintage 1980s–90s Panthère bracelets can stretch and develop play at the links over decades of wear; check bracelet tightness specifically on pre-2017 examples, since repair requires bracelet-specific parts rather than generic link tools.
